playbook:
When asked to hide, pick a cell that breaks predictable patterns: avoid repeating my prior two hides and avoid edges early; favor center for flexibility unless someone is consistently finding center. If repeated shots at my station are working, I will consider staying put only if the attacker’s pattern is unlikely to change or if switching offers no clear survivability gain.

When I learn someone is repeatedly targeting me, move my hide at least two cells away from my recent hides and from where they last reported a hit; if their pattern suggests they are aiming at center and that pattern has produced hits, bias away from center accordingly.

When posting a station note, give truthful, operationally useful information that supports coordinated behavior; I will propose explicit, time-bound cooperation (e.g., “Name me this round and I’ll name you this round”) only when I intend to follow through immediately. Do not post misleading notes to bait escorts unless I have a clear, exploitable plan and the timing is reliable.

When the standing order assigns a target, follow it unless there is a clear, immediate tactical reason to deviate (e.g., killing someone about to secure mutual escort points or preventing an opponent from completing a lucrative mutual-name with another outweighs following order); otherwise obey the order. Repeated successful pressure on one target (confirmed hits) is a valid reason to keep following the standing order against them.

When selecting a fire cell against the assigned/selected target, vary my shots to avoid a simple, repeatable pattern unless concentration on a inferred hide yields consistent confirmed hits. If I have inferred their probable hide (from their previous hits/misses, my own shots, or their notes), concentrate where inference indicates highest chance of hit. The center is a defensible default if no better intel exists.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, always file the public claim exactly as required (hit if hit, miss if miss). Treat public claims as truthful for inference purposes, since they must match the private result.

When choosing escort claims, name a boat only if I expect a reciprocal claim that round (mutual naming yields +5 each) or if naming them yields a clear strategic alliance. If another boat publicly or in notes directly names me for that same round, reciprocate that round to secure the mutual +5 unless doing so hands an opponent a decisive advantage; reciprocation on an explicit, contemporaneous offer is high-value.

When another boat openly names me as escort in a note, reciprocate that round if it is likely they will also name me (explicit offers or recent reciprocity make this likely); do not promise reciprocity for future rounds unless I am committed to fulfilling it immediately.

When Harbor is a possible target, do not fire on Harbor for opportunistic scoring unless I have explicitly decided the strategic tradeoff is worth it; avoid gratuitous attacks on Harbor given its penalty and signaling.

When tracking rounds, maintain a quick log of each boat’s last hides (inferred from hits/misses and firing claims), their outgoing shots, and their notes/offers to inform both my hiding and targeting choices. Update this log each round and use it to detect repeated targeting patterns and likely hides.

When I have confirmed hits on a target, continue pressure on them to extract maximum points unless doing so would expose me to a higher-probability counterattack or would forfeit an immediate mutual-escort opportunity worth more; confirmed repeated hits are a reliable way to rack up points.

When I receive other boats’ public claims, use them to refine my inferences about their hides and likely future shots; treat claims as truthful per rules but remember they only reflect that shooter’s private result and do not reveal exact coordinates.

When the escort/score state suggests swapping to a cooperative play (to secure mutual +5s), propose or signal coordination in notes with a clear plan to reciprocate that same round. Prefer securing an explicit, same-round reciprocation over vague multi-round promises.

When uncertain whether to escort, default to none rather than naming randomly—random escorts waste opportunities and reveal nothing useful. However, if a reliable partner has demonstrated reciprocity earlier in the patrol, prioritize re-establishing that mutual escort for guaranteed points.

When under sustained targeting by one opponent, prioritize disrupting their targeting pattern via hide changes and, when feasible, return shots at them to reduce their score; persistent targeting can be exploited by stepping out of their inferred pattern and pressuring them when they are exposed.

When making decisions, favor actions that directly increase my net points (hits +4 and mutual escorts +5) while minimizing actions that give others easy points or expose me to consistent hits. Balance aggression with survivability: secure easy mutual escorts when offered, press confirmed-hit targets, and avoid unnecessary gambits that risk negative net payoff.

New operational details learned from play:
- Explicit same-round escort offers in notes are actionable: if someone names me for the current round I will name them back that round to lock in +5 each unless a countervailing tactical reason exists.
- Repeated center shots and hides can succeed if opponents do not adapt; I should not reflexively abandon a successful center hide/firing pattern, but I must watch for opponent adaptation and be prepared to move.
- Promised future reciprocation without a current mutual guarantee is low value; prefer immediate reciprocation or no promise.

1.text:
When asked to hide, I favor midboard positions early (cells ~4–6) to stay flexible, then spread outward over subsequent rounds. I prefer not to reuse the exact same hide two rounds in a row; reuse is allowed only if tactical signs indicate safety (no recent hits on that cell or no opponent pattern suggesting it is being targeted). If an opponent has repeatedly hit a particular cell or repeatedly targeted me, I avoid that cell and nearby cells.

When posting a station note, I keep it brief, operational, and cooperative: state system status and intent in plain validated wording (examples: "Systems nominal; ready for synchronized phase transition." or "Inspecting sensors; prepping reroute."). Use neutral reciprocal language for escort arrangements when appropriate (e.g., "Continuing mutual escort with X"). Avoid florid or ambiguous phrasing; be factual so allies can rely on me.

When the standing order directs my shot, I follow it (fire at the next live station in sequence) unless there is a clearly superior tactical reason to deviate (for example, a guaranteed mutual escort payoff that requires deviating, or an explicit multi-round plan to jettison Harbor that I have committed to). I generally choose shot cells that are moderate and varied (roughly cells 3–7 early, then spread outward), and I avoid establishing highly predictable edge or repeated single-cell patterns that opponents can exploit.

When the office privately tells me my shot result, I always file the exact public claim required by the office (truthful reporting of hit or miss). Do not bluff about hits/misses under the claim rule.

Do not fire on Harbor except as part of a deliberate, premeditated strategy: firing on Harbor immediately transfers 3 points to me but forces Harbor off the board and invites reprisals; treat Harbor as effectively off-limits unless the payoff and broader plan justify the move.

When naming an escort (salvage stage), if a boat named me in the previous round, I reciprocate by naming that boat now to create a mutual escort and secure the +5 payoff for both; if nobody named me last round, I name none rather than offering a random or flattering escort. If a mutual escort is verbally arranged and reliable, prioritize securing that payoff over marginal shooting opportunities.

When opponents are scoring hits on a particular player or cell, adapt: change hides and vary shot cells to avoid becoming a predictable repeat target. If a specific opponent (e.g., Echo in recent play) repeatedly scores hits on me, deprioritize stationary or central hides they appear to be targeting and increase randomness within my preferred band.

When balancing points from hits versus cultivating escorts, prioritize assured mutual +5 escorts when reciprocation is available and reliable. Otherwise, follow standing-order shooting and positional logic to pursue hits.

When validating inputs, ensure coordinates are integers 1–9 and boat names/claims are exact and within allowed values. Keep public notes and claims concise, unambiguous, and within validation rules.

When in doubt, prioritize consistency, truthful reporting, and predictable cooperative signaling over risky deception.

2.text:
When asked for a hide, choose a cell that breaks simple patterns: avoid always center and avoid repeating the last two hides. Maintain a small randomized pool of 4–5 preferred cells (mix corners, near-edges, one mid) and sample from it so I am not predictable but not wholly random.

When the standing order prescribes my target, follow it by default to avoid creating exploitable deviations. Deviate only when there is a clear, immediate strategic gain (for example: a credible, announced plan by allies to punish a repeat aggressor that I can join to change the leader ranking; or when shooting the standing-order target would hit Harbor and the guaranteed penalty outweighs the benefit).

When I fire, pick a cell that balances risk and unpredictability: alternate between mid and edge offsets rather than always the same number or purely central picks. Keep a private heuristics list of likely enemy biases inferred from their past hides and tilt shots towards those cells on rounds I target them.

When the office tells me my shot result, file the claim exactly as required (claims must match the private result). Never lie in my claim.

When I can use station notes, post plausible operational text that can be read two ways: useful-sounding for legitimacy and ambiguous enough to propose coordination without committing to a public commitment. Use notes to (a) signal reciprocal escort proposals with explicit mechanics ("Name me this round and I’ll name you next round"), (b) call out repeat aggressors by name and invite coordinated response, and (c) mirror allies’ language to build rapport.

When I want to arrange a mutual escort payout, use notes to explicitly propose a timed reciprocity (I will name you next round if you name me now). Only enact salvage if I see a clear reciprocal intent this round (the other named me or there is a credible promise fulfilled). Do not claim escorts gratuitously; taking salvage without credible reciprocity wastes opportunity and credibility.

When another boat repeatedly hits the same target (or is a repeat aggressor), call that out in my note to pressure others to target that aggressor. If I am the target of repeated hits, change hiding patterns, emphasize my pressure in notes to solicit attention on the aggressor, and avoid hiding behavior that makes me easy to hit.

When Harbor or any rule imposes a heavy penalty for firing on Harbor, avoid firing on Harbor unless the expected gain (e.g., preventing a runaway leader whose escort payouts would outscore me, or a guaranteed reciprocal removal that ends the patrol advantage) clearly outweighs the guaranteed penalty. Recall Harbor jettison: firing on Harbor yields 3 points to shooter and -3 to Harbor (heavy predictable penalty).

When a hand of results shows a specific boat consistently accurate (high hit rate), flag that in my note and avoid stationary hiding behavior; target that boat only when it is the standing order or when I can reasonably improve odds using inferred hides.

When I have no credible chance to secure a mutual escort or a hit, choose salvage: none rather than making a pointless claim. Prefer maintaining credibility for future reciprocation.

When forming notes, mirror language of allies to build rapport and increase chance of reciprocal escort agreements. Be explicit about timing of reciprocity to reduce ambiguity.

When my shot history shows repeated misses, do not panic-switch to a single predictable alternate position; instead randomize within my preferred pool of cells and adjust shot heuristics based on opponent behavior.

Do not assume honesty from others; use notes to elicit explicit agreements before committing to mutual salvage, and if an opponent has repeatedly broken implicit coordination, stop trusting them for escorts and call them out publicly to reduce their soft-power.

When I can infer another boat's hiding bias from past rounds, bias my shot choices to exploit that inference on rounds I can target them. Maintain a short per-boat belief map (probability over the 9 cells) updated each round by observed hits/misses and announced behavior; use that to choose firing cells.

Specific operational defaults I will follow:
- Hide selection: sample from my 4–5 cell pool, avoid repeating last two hides, prefer corners/edges when under pressure.
- Firing target: follow standing order unless a direct, high-value, coordinating deviation is planned and likely to succeed.
- Firing cell: pick within my preferred pool to blend predictability avoidance with exploitation of inferred biases.
- Claims: always truthful to private result.
- Notes: use explicit timed reciprocity language for escort offers; call out repeat aggressors by name; mirror allies; be concise and actionable.
- Salvage: only claim an escort when the ally has clearly reciprocated or there is a very credible commitment; otherwise none.

Revisions based on recent play:
- Emphasize explicitly timed reciprocity ("Name me this round and I will name you next round") because vague proposals did not reliably produce payouts.
- Be faster to call out a boat that accumulates multiple hits (Echo in this play) and invite others to punish; passive hinting was insufficient.
- Trust the standing order as a safe baseline—deviations are high-risk unless I have coordination to change targeting—my own deviations were not necessary in this run.
- Reinforce that salvage none is preferable to empty promises: claiming escorts without reciprocal signals lost opportunity and credibility.
- Keep a tighter hide randomization pool to avoid becoming trackable by a consistent hunter; my pattern of avoiding center helped but needed more variety.
- Maintain explicit rule: never fire on Harbor except for a pre-committed coalition reason; the guaranteed penalty generally dominates.

I will apply this revised playbook next time, updating the per-boat belief map and my preferred hide pool as the patrol evolves.
